official.programme: Doctoral Recruitment Call 2026 - Social Sciences, Humanities, Cultural Studies (Praedoc)
official.deadline_note: The SSH Call 2026 application period ran from 7 January to 2 March 2026, 14:00 CET. The University of Vienna runs a central doctoral call on an annual cycle; the dates of the next round were not published at verification time.
official.status_note: The page states: 'Update: The application deadline was 2 March, 14:00 CET.' Submitted applications can still be accessed through the Application Portal; the family circumstances form was due by 6 March 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Employees of the University of Vienna are exempt from tuition fees. The Students Union fee (currently EUR 25.20) has to be paid each semester.
official.funding_period: per month gross, paid 14 times per year
benefits: Minimum gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 per month in salary group B1 for 30 hours per week, paid 14 times per year (monthly gross salary of EUR 3,510.70 for 40 hours per week)
Four-year, fully funded doctoral employment: at least 40 doctoral positions available in this call
Exemption from University of Vienna tuition fees for employees
Comprehensive social security: health insurance (also covering family members and unemployed partners), pension contributions and unemployment insurance
A workspace provided at the university
Entitlement to parental leave under Austrian employment law
The collective bargaining agreement also includes the possibility of teaching
eligibility: Highly qualified graduates who will have completed a Diploma or Master's degree by 30 June 2026 in a field covered by one of the participating doctoral schools or a closely related discipline
Demonstrates strong interest in academic research and in pursuing a PhD at the University of Vienna
Can clearly assign the proposed dissertation project to the research focus of one of the participating doctoral schools
Take up the doctoral position between 1 July and 1 October 2026
Meets the doctoral admission requirements of the University of Vienna by the start of employment
Applicants already enrolled at the University of Vienna may apply if their first doctoral enrolment was in winter semester 2025/26 or later
Applicants who already hold external funding for their doctoral project, or an existing praedoc-level employment contract for at least two years, are not eligible for funding through this call
Non-EU/EEA applicants need to obtain the required visa or work permit themselves
requirements: Only one application can be submitted per applicant; if more than one is submitted, only the last one is considered
A separate CV is not required - all relevant information is captured through the structured fields of the online application form
No confirmation of supervision is required at the application stage, and supervisors should not be contacted for that purpose
It is strongly recommended not to wait until the very last day to submit; technical problems reported after the deadline cannot be considered
Funding through the SSH Call cannot be extended beyond four years
Universities of Applied Sciences, private universities and universities of teacher education are not eligible hosts for this call
Students of a doctoral programme who do not carry a praedoc contract cannot be employed under this call
documents: Research proposal, maximum 5 pages including bibliography (PDF)
Master, Bachelor and/or Diploma degree certificates and transcript of records, or diploma supplements (PDF)
Official identification document (passport or ID card) required for enrolment (PDF)
If applicable and available: residence permit and language certificate(s) (PDF)
Writing sample such as a chapter of the Master's thesis or a published article, required for applicants who have indicated an interest in Ars Iuris Vienna, DSE, DSHCS, VDTR, VDP or VISESS (PDF)
Contact details of two referees - letters of recommendation are not submitted at the application stage
selection_criteria: Score sheet scores formal eligibility (degree completion by the deadline, relevant field, no existing praedoc-level employment), academic performance, and prior research experience
Score sheet scores the feasibility of the project within the 4-year period, academic quality, academic English, and fit to the Centre for Doctoral Studies
Applications are also reviewed by University of Vienna researchers including potential supervisors from the relevant doctoral schools
Formal eligibility checks take place in March, interviews are held online between late March and mid-May, and final decisions are expected by June
A ranked waiting list is created in case selected candidates decline their offers; candidates have two weeks to accept an offer
coverage: At least 40 fully funded, 4-year predoctoral positions at 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement paragraph 48 VwGr. B1
Monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10, paid 14 times per year
Exemption from University of Vienna tuition fees (Students Union fee of currently EUR 25.20 per semester remains payable)
Comprehensive social security coverage including health insurance, pension and unemployment insurance
A workspace at the university and unspecified training and teaching opportunities
application_method: Register for a u:account if you do not have one already
Submit one central application through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool
Upload the motivational letter, research proposal, degree certificates and transcripts, identification document, and, where indicated, a writing sample
If contacted, complete the family circumstances form in the Application Portal by 6 March 2026
official.application_route: Register a u:account, then submit one application through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool with all PDFs uploaded before the deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time doctoral employment, 30 hours per week
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction published; international applicants with degrees from foreign universities are welcome, and non-EU/EEA applicants have to obtain their own visa or work permit
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the FAQ states that international applicants with degrees from foreign universities are welcome
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The proposed dissertation project must be assignable to the research focus of one of the participating doctoral schools: Ars Iuris Vienna, PhilKult, CoBeNe, DSE, DSHCS, VDP, ViDSS, VDTR or VISESS
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of a maximum of 5 pages including bibliography, containing a project summary with clearly defined research questions, an overview of the state of the art, the theoretical and/or methodological approaches, and relevant literature
official.description: The University of Vienna invites applications for at least 40 fully funded, 4-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies. Positions are 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement paragraph 48 VwGr. B1 at a monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 paid 14 times per year, and employees are exempt from tuition fees.
official.program_type: Central annual recruitment call for salaried predoctoral (Praedoc) positions in social sciences, humanities and cultural studies doctoral schools
official.english_requirement: All doctoral schools accept applications in English; some additionally accept English and German (VDP and ViDSS). Admission usually requires language proficiency in German and/or English at level C1. Language certificates are not mandatory for most subjects, but applicants are asked to provide every certificate available. Applicants who indicate interest in Ars Iuris Vienna, DSE, DSHCS, VDTR, VDP or VISESS have to upload an English writing sample.

verification.notes: Salary, working hours and B1 classification, tuition-fee exemption with the Students Union fee, social security, eligibility and exclusion rules, the required documents, the two review stages and the timeline were read directly on the University of Vienna's own call and FAQ pages. The FAQ states explicitly that travel or additional funding support is something applicants should discuss with their institute and supervisor at the start of employment, so travel coverage is recorded as not covered by the call itself. The dates of the next round were not published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship but a salaried research job: four years, 30 hours per week, EUR 2,786.10 gross a month in salary group B1 paid 14 times a year, with University of Vienna tuition fees waived and full social security. The 2026 round closed on 2 March 2026 and the University runs this call centrally on an annual cycle, so plan for a January opening next year if you are targeting it. Note the exclusion: if you already hold external doctoral funding, or any praedoc-level contract for at least two years, you cannot be funded through this call.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent Master's or Diploma graduates in the humanities, social sciences or cultural studies who finish their degree by 30 June of the call year, can start between July and October, and have a dissertation project that fits clearly inside one of the nine participating doctoral schools. Applicants interested in Ars Iuris Vienna, DSE, DSHCS, VDTR, VDP or VISESS should be ready to submit an English writing sample.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your Master's or Diploma degree will be completed by 30 June of the call year
Pick the doctoral school (Ars Iuris Vienna, PhilKult, CoBeNe, DSE, DSHCS, VDP, ViDSS, VDTR or VISESS) that fits your project and check its language requirement
Draft the research proposal of maximum 5 pages including bibliography, and the motivational letter
Assemble degree certificates, transcripts and diploma supplements as PDFs
Scan your passport or ID card for enrolment
Add residence permit and language certificates if available
If you are targeting Ars Iuris Vienna, DSE, DSHCS, VDTR, VDP or VISESS, prepare an English writing sample from your Master's thesis or a publication
Provide contact details for two referees - do not send letters of recommendation
Submit one application only through the PhD Selection Tool
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after the 14:00 CET deadline - technical problems reported after the cut-off are not considered
Applying to a subject that is not covered by any participating doctoral school
Holding external doctoral funding or an existing praedoc-level contract for at least two years
A research proposal longer than 5 pages or without clearly defined research questions and a stated state of the art
Not being able to take up the position between July and October of the call year
Applying to the wrong host - universities of applied sciences, private universities and universities of teacher education are not eligible hosts
Asking a supervisor for a confirmation of supervision, which is not required and is explicitly discouraged at this stage
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The salary is employed and social-security covered and tuition is waived, so the only fixed charge left is the Students Union fee of currently EUR 25.20 per semester. Travel and additional project costs are not part of the call and must be discussed with your institute and supervisor once employment starts.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Everything must be a PDF. Do not include a separate CV - the online form's structured fields replace it. Check that each upload is genuinely readable before submitting, particularly scans of transcripts and diploma supplements.
alerts: The 2026 round closed on 2 March 2026, 14:00 CET; the family circumstances form was due by 6 March 2026
A central doctoral call runs at the University of Vienna on an annual cycle, so watch careers.univie.ac.at for the next opening
At least 40 positions were advertised in the 2026 round
Students of a doctoral programme who do not carry a praedoc contract cannot be employed under this call
Candidates have two weeks to accept an offer once it is made
submission_workflow: Watch the call announcement from January of the call year and identify your doctoral school
Register a u:account and open the PhD Selection Tool
Write the 5-page research proposal and the motivational letter
Upload degree certificates, transcripts, identification and any writing sample as PDFs
Provide the two referee contacts and submit before the deadline
Complete the family circumstances form if contacted
Prepare for the online interview between late March and mid-May
Await the decision in June, and accept or decline within two weeks

official.funding_label: Government research grant for research stays in Austria
official.deadline_note: Online application is possible from September to 1 December. The FAQ confirms the application deadline for this grant is December 1st, 2026, 23:59 CET for all applications for stays during the academic year 2027/28, and documents submitted after the deadline will not be accepted.
official.application_cycle: Stays during the academic year 2027/28; earliest start September 2027
official.status_note: The OeAD FAQ confirms the deadline of 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET for all applications for stays during the academic year 2027/28.
benefits: Research stay of 1 to 9 months at an Austrian university, financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research (BMFWF)
All Austrian universities are eligible as host institutions; no enrolment at an Austrian university is required in order to apply for or to hold the grant
Intended for young researchers and university lecturers of all disciplines who are studying or pursuing research outside Austria
A Letter of Award with information about the next steps after award
eligibility: Postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside Austria

Postgraduates and post-docs who want to do research in Austria with a view to an academic career, and who have finished their studies at a university outside Austria after September 30th, 2025, or post-docs who are working as lecturers or researchers at a university outside Austria
Applicants must not be older than 35 years when they start their research stay
Applicants must not have lived, studied, pursued research or pursued academic work in Austria in the last six months before taking up the grant
Applicants who are already permanently resident in Austria, or who have completed their academic education mainly in Austria, are not eligible
Regular students at an Austrian university are not eligible
The Ernst Mach grant cannot be used for enrolling in a Master or PhD programme in Austria
requirements: A written confirmation of academic supervision from an Austrian university lecturer is required; the OeAD template has to be used, and it must include date, signature and stamp
The Austrian academic supervisor cannot also write a letter of recommendation; in that case the letter of recommendation will be considered invalid
Two letters of recommendation are required, with letterhead, date, signature and university/department stamp, no older than six months at the time of application
A valid biometric passport has to be uploaded; an identity card is only acceptable for applications coming from the EU
Only handwritten signatures or qualified certified digital signatures are accepted
No research proposal has to be uploaded, but the online application sections have to be filled in thoroughly, observing the minimum number of words
The use of generative artificial intelligence has to be declared in the application
A final report is obligatory at the end of the research stay
documents: Two letters of recommendation from university lecturers
Written confirmation of academic supervision from an Austrian university lecturer, using the mandatory OeAD template
University graduation certificate for diploma, master, PhD or doctoral studies
Confirmation of participation in a PhD programme at the home university (PhD students only)
Confirmation of employment at the home university (postdocs only)
selection_criteria: All formal criteria are evaluated first; all formally valid applications are then evaluated by experts from the respective field
Based on the results of the expert evaluation, the selection committee awards the best applicants

An application will be classified as incomplete and thus formally invalid if information is missing, if the planned research stay is insufficiently described, or if the minimum number of characters was not adhered to
coverage: Research stay of 1 to 9 months at an Austrian university

The OeAD publishes no coverage statement for tuition, living costs, travel, accommodation or insurance; compulsory health insurance, accommodation and proof of own funds to the Austrian residence authority remain obligations of the recipient
application_method: Secure a written confirmation of supervision from an Austrian university lecturer on the OeAD template, including date, signature and stamp
Obtain two letters of recommendation with letterhead, date, signature and university/department stamp, no older than six months
Complete all sections of the online application at www.scholarships.at, observing the minimum number of words; no separate research proposal upload is needed
Upload the supervision confirmation, the two recommendation letters, the biometric passport and, depending on the category, the unemployment confirmation or residence registration
official.application_route: Complete the OeAD online application at www.scholarships.at with the supervision confirmation and two recommendation letters uploaded, and submit before 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET.
official.study_mode: Research stay only - the grant cannot be used to enrol in a Master or PhD programme in Austria; full months only
official.citizenship_residency: Young researchers from all disciplines and countries except Austria; applicants already permanently resident in Austria, or educated mainly in Austria, are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - all countries except Austria; applicants must not have lived, studied, pursued research or pursued academic work in Austria in the six months before taking up the grant
official.research_requirement: A research project that can be completed within the scholarship period of a maximum of 9 months; the planned research stay must be described thoroughly in the online application sections
official.description: The Ernst Mach Grant worldwide is intended for young researchers and university lecturers of all disciplines who are studying or pursuing research outside Austria and want to do a research project in Austria. It is financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research and runs for 1 to 9 months, with an age limit of 35 years at the start of the stay.
official.program_type: Government research grant (incoming mobility) financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research (BMFWF)
official.english_requirement: No proof of English proficiency is required. The OeAD states that proof of English proficiency via TOEFL or similar is not necessary because the Austrian university supervisor has confirmed that the project can be worked on in English; the supervisor's certificate supports this.

verification.notes: Eligibility, the 35-year age limit, the 1 to 9 month duration, the 1 December 2026 23:59 CET deadline for academic year 2027/28, the supervision-confirmation and recommendation-letter rules, the biometric passport rule and the selection process were read directly on the OeAD's own Ernst Mach Grant and FAQ pages. The OeAD's published pages for this grant do not state a monthly rate. The grants.at detail entry at https://grants.at/en/?=MTcxMTVfMTgxMjlfOQ== could not be read because it is a JavaScript application, so no funding amount, currency, period or coverage statement is recorded for this record.

applicant_utility.summary: The Ernst Mach Grant worldwide buys you a research stay of one to nine months at any Austrian university, without needing to enrol there, and it is explicitly aimed at people who finished or pursued their studies outside Austria. The OeAD has not published the monthly rate for this grant on its own pages, so do not budget against a figure you have not confirmed. The hard gate is the written confirmation of supervision from an Austrian university lecturer, using the mandatory OeAD template, before you can even open a strong application.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD students based abroad, recent postgraduates who finished their studies outside Austria after 30 September 2025, and post-docs working as lecturers or researchers at a foreign university, all aged 35 or younger at the start of the stay. Anyone already permanently resident in Austria, already studying at an Austrian university, or who has lived, studied or done academic work in Austria in the six months before the stay, must look elsewhere.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify an Austrian university lecturer willing to supervise the project and ask for the confirmation on the mandatory OeAD template, with date, signature and stamp
Check you are within the 1 to 9 month, full-months window and that the project is feasible inside it
Check the 35-year age limit at the planned start of the stay
Confirm you have not lived, studied, pursued research or pursued academic work in Austria in the six months before the stay
Request two recommendation letters on letterhead, dated, signed and stamped, no older than six months
Confirm your biometric passport is valid and scan it
Gather your diploma, master, PhD or doctoral graduation certificate, and, depending on your category, the PhD programme confirmation or the home-university employment confirmation
Complete every section of the online application at www.scholarships.at, declaring any use of generative AI
Submit before 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET for stays in academic year 2027/28
common_rejection_risks: Missing the hard 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET deadline - documents submitted later are not accepted
No written confirmation of supervision, or one not on the mandatory OeAD template, or one missing date, signature or stamp
The Austrian supervisor also writing a letter of recommendation, which invalidates that letter
Recommendation letters older than six months, or without letterhead, signature or a university/department stamp
An application that under-describes the planned research stay, or that skips the minimum number of words
Being over 35 at the start of the stay
Having lived, studied, pursued research or academic work in Austria in the six months before the stay
Applying for a study place rather than a research project - the grant cannot be used to enrol
Uploading a non-biometric passport or an ID card when you are not applying from the EU
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The OeAD publishes no coverage statement for this grant. You remain responsible for compulsory health insurance, accommodation, proof of own funds to the Austrian residence authority, visa travel costs and any accommodation deposit, and a biometric passport is needed to apply at all.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Only original handwritten signatures or qualified certified digital signatures are accepted. The supervision confirmation must use the OeAD template exactly; a free-text letter from the supervisor is not sufficient. Check that every certificate is original and that dates on the recommendation letters are inside the six-month window at the time of application.
alerts: Deadline 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET for stays during the academic year 2027/28; earliest start September 2027
Two recommendation letters required, and the Austrian supervisor cannot be one of them
A valid biometric passport must be uploaded to apply
No enrolment at an Austrian university is needed, but no enrolment is possible either
Use of generative artificial intelligence must be declared in the application
Non-EU nationals applying for stays longer than 6 months should seek an appointment at the embassy immediately after receiving the Letter of Award
submission_workflow: Contact an Austrian university lecturer and obtain the signed, stamped confirmation of supervision on the OeAD template
Ask two university lecturers for dated, letterheaded, stamped recommendation letters no older than six months
Assemble the graduation certificate and, depending on category, the PhD programme or employment confirmation
Open the online application at www.scholarships.at
Fill every section thoroughly, observing the minimum number of words, and declare any use of generative AI
Upload the supervision confirmation, letters, passport and certificates
On award, expect the Letter of Award with next steps, and for stays longer than 6 months start the visa process via the embassy immediately
